subject: Reserved GPU footprint: VectorLex pre-commit sizing & negotiation
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@vectorlex.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: VectorLex Procurement <procurement@vectorlex.ai>, Tom Muller <tom.muller@cloudops.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing inputs for reserved fleet (VectorLex)

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team reviewed Redwood's reserved-capacity model and we'd like to move toward a preliminary commitment discussion. Before legal/procurement get involved we want a short, concrete sizing estimate so we know what order of magnitude to expect for monthly committed spend.

High level about VectorLex:
- Production: search + RAG assistant for enterprise legal docs (multi-tenant across 120 accounts)
- Typical session: single-query search or short chat (prompt ~180 tokens, response ~220 tokens)
- Peak concurrent sessions: currently ~4,500 user-facing sessions during business hours; expected 2.5x growth within 9 months
- Burst events: monthly index-refresh days where throughput spikes ~3x for ~4 hours

We attached a small telemetry sample (vectorlex_telemetry_sample.csv) and would appreciate a short worksheet showing:
1) a conservative reserved GPU footprint (GPU SKUs + count) to meet P95 latency targets for interactive queries (<= 300ms token latency)
2) burst handling approach and required burst capacity
3) recommended canary/rollout plan for an initial 3-week pilot

Can you take a look and loop in whoever should be on sizing? We'd like a one-pager by early next week if possible.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product Operations
VectorLex

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@vectorlex.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for reserved fleet (VectorLex)

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the telemetry extract. Attaching a short sizing worksheet and a quick sketch of options (redwood_sizing_summary_v1.pdf).

High-level takeaways from our quick pass:
- Baseline interactive footprint: ~18 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved) to sustain 4,500 P95-interactive requests with the prompt/response sizes you gave, assuming ~40% KV cache hit rate and continuous batching tuned to 20ms queue target. This is the conservative reserved commit.
- Burst plan: reserve an additional 6 GPUs for predictable bursts (policy-based burst from dedicated pool) + an ability to autoscale an extra 8 GPUs on hosted capacity for rare peak events (3x spikes).
- Pilot recommendation (3 weeks): start with 8 reserved GPUs + burst capacity (6 reserved burst slots) for a staged rollout across 3 accounts; use telemetry-derived prompts for regression checks; measure token latency and throughput over first 7 days before scaling to full reservation.

Open questions that materially affect the sizing:
- True KV cache effectiveness (40% is our working estimate; if you can confirm prefix-reuse numbers we can tighten the footprint by ~20%)
- Average prompt/response variances across product lines (the sample looks narrowly centered at 180/220; if some flows produce 1k+ tokens that changes occupancy significantly)
- SLA targets beyond latency (99th percentile tail latency vs P95 — we sized to P95; if you need 99th at the same headroom we should add ~30% more GPUs)

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll run a quick cost/latency sensitivity (two scenarios: conservative commit vs aggressive stage) and share a one-page matrix by Monday morning.
2) Marissa will model the occupancy/burst economics and produce a short MUP (monthly unit price) estimate.
3) Karthik will scope the canary rollout and what telemetry we need to validate perf and quality.

Attaching the sizing summary and a mutual action plan (MAP) draft — see the attachments list. If that timeline works I'll sync back with the one-pager and a recommended PO structure that Procurement can use.

Cheers,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@vectorlex.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: VectorLex Procurement <procurement@vectorlex.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 08:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for reserved fleet (VectorLex)

Avery — thanks for the quick pass. A couple clarifications after we pulled more telemetry:
- The 4,500 concurrent figure was conservative for peak search; after re-segmenting traffic we see ~3,300 sustained interactive sessions across primary tenants during business hours, but some enterprise customers have heavier batch-style workflows that produce 5–10x longer responses (these are 2% of overall traffic).
- Our prefix-reuse/KV cache hit looks closer to 55% for search (better than your estimate), but only ~20% for the chat flows.

I'm attaching an expanded CSV with sample long-response traces. Can you update the one-pager to show:
A) a reserved-commit estimate that assumes 3,300 sustained interactive (with 55% KV hit for search) but includes a separate sizing line for the long-response batch flows (showing incremental GPUs required if those flows move to production)?
B) an explicit fallback policy recommendation — i.e., how we should route to hosted compatible quantized models during sustained overruns to avoid SLA violations.

We'd like the short deck by EOD Wednesday if possible; legal/procurement want an initial number to fast-track internal approvals.

Thanks —
Elena

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@vectorlex.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, VectorLex Procurement <procurement@vectorlex.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing inputs for reserved fleet (VectorLex)

Elena / Procurement team —

Attached is an updated one-pager and the mutual action plan (MAP) with explicit milestones (mutual_action_plan_v2.docx). Summary here so procurement/legal can quickly see the ask:

Summary recommendation (conservative baseline + incremental options):
- Baseline reserved commit (production interactive): 12 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs reserved. Rationale: assumes 3,300 sustained interactive sessions, 55% KV hit on search paths, continuous batching with 25ms queue target to preserve P95 token latency <= 300ms.
- Incremental batch-safe buffer: +4 A100-equiv GPUs to absorb long-response batch flows (the 2% heavy flows). These can be reserve+burst or staged onto a reserve pool separated by template (tenant segregation).
- Burst / peak handling: 6 reserved burst slots (kept cold) + hosted autoscale allowance up to 10 GPUs for rare 3x events. Bursts will be governed by policy: when queue depth exceeds configured thresholds, route matched prompts to quantized hosted variants (lower cost, slightly lower quality) per fallback policy.
- Canary / pilot plan (3 weeks): start with 6 reserved GPUs and pre-configured 3-burst slots; run across 3 tenants, validate P95 latency, KV cache effectiveness, and end-to-end cost per 1M tokens. If metrics meet acceptance after 7 days, expand to baseline reserve.

Commercial and operational notes:
- Suggested commitment term: 12 months with a 60-day ramp window (credits if we miss agreed SLAs during ramp).
- Proposed pricing sheet attached (MUP options included) — Marissa modeled two pricing bands (standard reserved vs reserved+burst).
- Required inputs from VectorLex to finalize: 7-day token histogram by tenant, target P99 latency (if different from P95), and confirmation of restrictable data residency (for private deployment considerations).

Next steps:
1) VectorLex to confirm which tenants will be in the pilot and share the 7-day token histogram (Procurement + Product).
2) Redwood to produce a final SOW and draft PO template for Procurement to review (we'll include the MAP milestones).
3) Legal to review the draft commitment terms (I'll loop our contracts lead once Procurement signals go-ahead).

If you want, I can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk Procurement through the one-pager.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[attachments: redwood_sizing_summary_v1.pdf; mutual_action_plan_v2.docx; vectorlex_telemetry_sample.csv]
